source.quote: we have decided to push back the deprecation date to November 12, 2025.

tasks.reasoning:
This one task covers all 3 slack changes that affect this repo. Handle every one of them in this single change set, prove each with your test, and say in finish which you changed and which needed no change.

1. files.upload API method sunset (deadline pushed to Nov 12, 2025); migrate to files.getUploadURLExternal / files.completeUploadExternal (files_upload_v2 in Python SDK) (endpoint-removed, effective 2025-11-12)
   Source: https://docs.slack.dev/changelog
   Quote: we have decided to push back the deprecation date to November 12, 2025.
   Affects: operations: files.upload, files_upload
   Call sites: Tableau2Slack.py:99 (Calls WebClient.files_upload (files.upload) with channels/file/title/filetype to post the Tableau view image. Slack sunsets files.upload on 2025-11-12, so after that date every run fails to upload the image.)
   Why it applies: The repo uploads the rendered Tableau image with files_upload, which hits the files.upload method being sunset on 2025-11-12. It must move to files.getUploadURLExternal plus files.completeUploadExternal, normally through files_upload_v2. The code also reads file.url_private from the response. files_upload_v2 returns a 'files' list (and 'file' only for a single upload), so the migration agent must check how the URL is read and, if it is referenced in chat_postMessage, confirm the URL is still valid. files_upload_v2 takes 'channel' (a single ID) instead of 'channels'. Dependency: slackclient==2.5.0 has no files_upload_v2; it exists only in slack_sdk>=3.19. So this task depends on the slack_sdk v3 migration task. The alternative is to call the two external-upload endpoints directly via api_call in 2.5.0. After the sunset, image delivery to Slack breaks outright.

2. PyPI slackclient (2.x) is in maintenance mode; successor slack_sdk v3 renames the package, deprecates `slack.*` imports, drops required aiohttp and changes WebClient (no run_async) (sdk-major, effective 2020-11)
   Source: https://docs.slack.dev/tools/python-slack-sdk/v3-migration/
   Quote: The PyPI project has been renamed from slackclient to slack_sdk.
   Affects: operations: WebClient, LegacyWebClient, AsyncWebClient, run_async; versions: <3.0.0, 3.0.0; sdk: slackclient
   Call sites: Tableau2Slack.py:96 (Builds WebClient from the slackclient 2.x package (slack.* import). This must become 'from slack_sdk import WebClient' with the slack_sdk requirement replacing slackclient==2.5.0.); Tableau2Slack.py:99 (The files_upload call runs through the upgraded client. slack_sdk>=3.19 is required for files_upload_v2, which the files.upload sunset task needs.); Tableau2Slack.py:141 (The chat_postMessage call runs through the upgraded client. The API is unchanged, but it needs verifying after the package swap.)
   Why it applies: The repo pins slackclient==2.5.0, which is deprecated and in maintenance mode. Its successor slack_sdk v3 renames the package and deprecates slack.* imports. The repo does not use run_async or aiohttp, so the change is mainly the dependency and import swap. This upgrade is also the prerequisite for files_upload_v2, which the files.upload sunset task needs. The deadline is therefore tied to that 2025-11-12 sunset; the original rename was in 2020-11.

3. Classic apps deprecation: date pushed repeatedly (to May 25, 2026), later paused; still recommended to migrate to Slack apps; new classic apps cannot be created (product-shutdown, effective 2026-05-25)
   Source: https://slack.dev/blog/slack-developer-changelog-recap-october-december-2025
   Quote: Classic apps will continue to work for the foreseeable future, but they’re still considered a legacy integration method with Slack and new classic apps cannot be created.
   Call sites: Tableau2Slack.py:96 (The WebClient uses a bot token whose app type (classic vs modern Slack app) is unknown. The project dates from the classic-app era.)
   Why it applies: Uncertain. The repo authenticates with a bot token, and the code does not show whether the token comes from a classic app. Classic app retirement was pushed to 2026-05-25 and then paused, and Slack still recommends migrating. The migration agent should check the setup docs or README for the app type. If it is a classic app, document migrating to a modern Slack app with granular scopes (chat:write, files:write). This is unlikely to need code changes beyond a token swap.

The files_upload call runs through the upgraded client. slack_sdk>=3.19 is required for files_upload_v2, which the files.upload sunset task needs.

record.prBody:
## 3 changes: files.upload API method sunset (deadline pushed to Nov 12, 2025); migrate to files.getUploadURLExternal / files.completeUploadExternal (files_upload_v2 in Python SDK) and more [Verified]

### Change

Swapped slackclient==2.5.0 for slack_sdk>=3.19.0,<4 (imports now slack_sdk). Replaced files_upload with files_upload_v2 (channel ID from new env var slackUploadChannelId, filetype dropped, response parsed via file or files[0]). chat_postMessage unchanged. Added slackUploadChannelId to example.env and tests/test_slack_sdk.py (AST + import test). Classic-app item: needed no code change; app type can't be determined from code. If the token is from a classic app, recreate as a modern app with scopes files:write, chat:write, chat:write.customize (needed for username/icon_url). Bot must be a member of the upload channel. Docs (documentation/1-gettingstarted.md line 33 and the Medium article) still say to create a #tableau-test channel; left unchanged and should be updated to mention the channel ID.

Files touched:
- `Tableau2Slack.py`
- `example.env`
- `requirements.txt`
- `tests/test_slack_sdk.py`

### Why

files.upload is sunset on 2025-11-12, and slackclient 2.5.0 has no files_upload_v2, so the SDK had to move to slack_sdk 3.19 or later.

> we have decided to push back the deprecation date to November 12, 2025.

Source: https://docs.slack.dev/changelog

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| slack-sdk-test | fail (1) | pass | 0 |

New failures: 0

Checks added by the agent (they count toward proof; check that each command really tests the change):
- slack-sdk-test, added by the agent: `python tests/test_slack_sdk.py` (fail (1) → pass)

Provider validators: none run.

Test of this change: `slack-sdk-test`, written by the agent and run with the checks.

Where checks ran: Docker container python:3.12-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- Real files_upload_v2 response shape and whether url_private works immediately in the following chat_postMessage attachment
- Whether the bot token belongs to a classic app
- Docs still mention the #tableau-test channel name
- No provider validator was run.

### Behaviour changes

- New required env var slackUploadChannelId (channel ID, not #name); the old hardcoded #tableau-test is gone
- filetype=png removed; Slack infers the type
- files_upload_v2 is asynchronous on Slack's side, so the file may take a moment to be available

---

review.summary: The diff swaps files_upload for files_upload_v2 and moves imports to slack_sdk, which is the right migration. It also adds a new required env var, and the 'verified' grade rests on an AST/hasattr test that never exercises the upload path. The chat_postMessage call site is unchanged, and the diff only fixes its import. Pre-existing: the bare `except:` swallows errors and the script runs on import.

concerns.issue: The new env var slackUploadChannelId is read with os.getenv and no validation. If it is unset, files_upload_v2 gets channel=None. Depending on the SDK version, it either skips sharing or raises, and the bare `except:` or the SlackApiError handler then hides the failure. Existing deployments with an old .env will break silently after upgrading. The old code used the hardcoded name '#tableau-test', which was a name rather than an ID, so this is a config change beyond the API change.

The old flow relied on files_upload sharing the file into a channel and returning file.url_private. files_upload_v2 returns a response with 'file' and 'files' keys, and the `img.get('file') or img['files'][0]` fallback is defensive. I could not confirm from the diff that url_private is populated immediately after completeUploadExternal. Check the SDK response shape or run a live call. The attachments image_url depends on this value.

The test only parses the source with ast and checks that the WebClient has the attributes. It makes no mocked or live call to Slack, so the channel argument, response parsing and url_private extraction are untested. The 'after pass' result proves only that the imports and method names changed. It is also a bare script with asserts, not a pytest function, and it ignores the Tableau2Slack() call that runs on import.

Moving from slackclient 2.5.0 to slack_sdk >=3.19.0,<4 is a large jump. WebClient(slackBotToken) positional token still works. The pinned old dependencies (nest-asyncio 1.3.3, requests 2.22.0) were not checked for compatibility with the new SDK. files_upload_v2 needs at least 3.19, which matches the lower bound.
The filetype='png' parameter was dropped. files_upload_v2 infers the type from the filename or accepts a filename argument, so this is likely fine, but the title or filename of the upload may change.
